title: BA-26-030-NL-Tilbygg Mariringen barnehage
description: Nordre Land kommune skal utvide og oppgradere Mariringen barnehage på Torpa. Anskaffelsen gjelder tilbygg, påbygg og rehabilitering av deler av eksisterende bygningsmasse, og gjennomføres som en totalentreprise etter NS 8407 med totalentreprenørens prosjekteringsansvar. Arbeidene er beskrevet som en funksjonsbeskrivelse. Barnehagen har i dag to avdelinger med plass til 60 barn. Kapasiteten utvides med en tredje avdeling. Eksisterende bygg er en trebygning med saltak, med ca. 340 m² BTA i første etasje og ca. 75 m² i andre etasje. Kontrakten omfatter: * nytt tilbygg for oppstilling av barnevogner i nordvest, ca. 30 m² * tilbygg for ny avdeling i sørøst, ca. 145 m², med baseareal, garderober og sanitærrom * påbygg i andre etasje med personal- og møterom med kjøkken og lager, ca. 30 m² * oppgradering av eldre del av eksisterende bygg: gulvbelegg, veggoverflater, dører og felles kjøkken * riving av eksisterende utebod og bygging av ny utebod med overdekket areal for uteopphold * tilpasninger på uteområdet * VVS-, elkraft-, tele- og automatiseringsinstallasjoner, inkludert ny ventilasjon, gulvvarme og tilknytning til byggherrens SD-anlegg Barnehagedriften flyttes til midlertidige lokaler i byggeperioden. Oppdragsgiver har lagt til grunn en byggetid på tre måneder. Entreprisen omfatter seks måneders prøvedrift etter overtakelse. Oppdragsgiver planlegger å holde en felles befaring 26. november 2026. Tid og sted kunngjøres som tilleggsinformasjon.

title: Netherlands – Pollution investigation services – PFAS bronnenonderzoek 2027 in werkgebied ODWH
description: Omgevingsdienst West-Holland (ODWH) is voornemens een raamovereenkomst te sluiten met een opdrachtnemer voor het uitvoeren van PFAS-bronnenonderzoek binnen haar werkgebied. De opdracht omvat het voorbereiden, uitvoeren en rapporteren van bodemonderzoek op PFAS-verdachte locaties. De werkzaamheden bestaan onder meer uit historisch onderzoek, locatiebezoeken, het opstellen van onderzoeksstrategieën, veldwerk, bemonstering, laboratoriumanalyses en het beoordelen en rapporteren van de onderzoeksresultaten. Het doel is inzicht te verkrijgen in de aanwezigheid, herkomst, verspreiding en mogelijke risico's van PFAS-verontreinigingen voor mens en milieu. Voor 2027 wordt uitgegaan van circa twintig onderzoekslocaties. De opdracht betreft het uitvoeren van PFAS-bronnenonderzoek op circa twintig locaties in 2027 binnen het werkgebied van Omgevingsdienst West-Holland (ODWH). Het daadwerkelijke aantal onderzoekslocaties is afhankelijk van de benodigde onderzoeksinspanning en het beschikbare budget. De geraamde waarde van de raamovereenkomst bedraagt € 220.000 exclusief btw over de volledige looptijd, inclusief de eventuele verlenging. De maximale waarde van de raamovereenkomst bedraagt € 330.000 exclusief btw, inclusief de eventuele verlenging. Er geldt geen afnamegarantie.

title: MOD FM Maintenance East Anglia
description: We are seeking expressions of interest from experienced Facilities Management providers to support the delivery of Facilities Maintenance services across the East Anglia region as part of the Ministry of Defence (MOD) Future Defence Infrastructure Services (FDIS) contract. The anticipated annual contract value is approximately £6 million per annum, with potential for additional workload and revenue growth subject to operational requirements, contract performance, and future programme demands. The successful supplier will be responsible for the delivery of planned preventative maintenance, reactive maintenance, and associated facilities engineering services across a diverse estate portfolio. Services are expected to cover a broad range of mechanical and electrical building systems and associated infrastructure. Scope of Services The scope is expected to include, but is not limited to: Mechanical maintenance services Electrical maintenance services Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) Reactive and corrective maintenance Statutory and mandatory compliance activities Out-of-hours and emergency response services Minor lifecycle and maintenance works Asset inspection, reporting and condition assessments Supplier Profile This opportunity is likely to be best suited to an established Mechanical and Electrical Facilities Management provider with: Demonstrable experience delivering facilities maintenance services within complex and operationally critical environments. Strong self-delivery capability across mechanical and electrical disciplines. An established directly employed workforce capable of delivering the majority of maintenance activities. Existing operational presence within, or close to, the East Anglia region. The ability to mobilise and sustain a locally based workforce to support service delivery requirements. Robust health, safety, environmental and compliance management systems. Whilst organisations of all sizes are encouraged to express an interest, SMEs with a strong self-delivery model and established local engineering resource are particularly encouraged to participate. Key Requirements Prospective suppliers should be able to demonstrate: Relevant facilities management and maintenance experience. Financial stability appropriate to the scale of the opportunity. Proven performance in delivering maintenance services against contractual KPIs and service levels. Capability to operate in secure and regulated environments. Commitment to social value, local employment and skills development within the East Anglia region. Additional Information This notice is being issued to assess market interest and identify suitably qualified suppliers capable of supporting the delivery of facilities maintenance services under the MOD FDIS programme. Further information regarding procurement route, detailed scope and contractual arrangements will be provided at the appropriate stage of the procurement process.

buyer: Suomen urheilun eettinen keskus SUEK ry
title: Dopingnäytteiden kuljetuspalveluiden hankinta
description: Suomen urheilun eettinen keskus SUEK ry (jäljempänä "SUEK") pyytää tarjousta dopingnäytteiden kuljetuspalveluista. Kilpailutus on jaettu kahteen osa-alueeseen: Osa-alue 1 Peruskuljetuspalvelut eli dopingnäytteiden (virtsa- ja verinäytteet) kuljettaminen laboratorioon Osa-alue 2 Erikoiskuljetuspalvelut eli dopingnäytteiden (virtsa- ja verinäytteet) kuljettaminen laboratorioon siten, että kuljetuspalveluihin kohdistuu peruskuljetuspalveluista poikkeavia erityisjärjestelyjä (mm. poikkeava ajankohta, lähetyspaikka, kriittinen kuljetusaikataulu). Tarjoaja voi antaa tarjoukseen yhteen tai molempiin osa-alueisiin. Kumpaankin osa-alueeseen valitaan yksi (1) palveluntuottaja. Palveluntuottajan kanssa tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa oleva sopimus siten, että sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on kevät 2027. SUEK arvioi, että dopingnäytteiden kuljetuksista yli 90 % kohdistuu Suomen sisällä Helsingissä sijaitsevaan laboratorioon. Loput kuljetuksista toimitetaan muualle Eurooppaan. Selvyyden vuoksi todetaan, että SUEK tilaa tarjouspyynnön mukaisia kuljetuspalveluita tosiasiallisen tarpeensa mukaan. SUEK ei sitoudu sopimuskauden aikana tiettyihin tilausmääriin, eikä sopimus tuota valitulle palveluntuottajalle yksinoikeutta tarjota kuljetuspalveluita SUEKille. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä. , Osa-alue 1 Peruskuljetuspalvelut Osa-alue 1 (Peruskuljetuspalvelut) koskee dopingnäytteiden (virtsa- ja verinäytteet) kuljettamista laboratorioon. Palveluntuottajan tulee antaa tarjous myös peruskuljetuspalveluista ulkomaille siten, kuin tarjouspyynnössä on tarkemmin määritelty. SUEKin tämänhetkisen arvioin mukaan peruskuljetuspalveluiden mukaisia lähetyksiä on noin 50–60 kappaletta kuukaudessa siten, että yhden lähetyksen paino on noin 2-8 kg. SUEK ei kuitenkaan ole sidottu mihinkään tilausmääriin, vaan hyödyntää kuljetuspalveluita tosiasiallisen tarpeensa mukaan. Palveluntuottajan tulee tarjota alusta, jonka avulla SUEKilla on mahdollisuus luoda ja tulostaa rahtikirjoja tai luoda muita vaihtoehtoisia lähetystunnuksia (esim. sähköinen QR-koodi) itse. Tarvittaessa palveluntuottaja tuottaa palvelun SUEKin puolesta (eli luo/tulostaa rahtikirjat tai QR-koodit) ilman erillisiä kustannuksia. Ko. rahtikirjojen/lähetystunnusten tulee olla voimassa vähintään kuusi (6) kuukautta niiden luomisesta lukien. SUEK huolehtii näytteiden pakkaamisesta SUEKin omiin sinetöityihin kuljetuslaukkuihin, joissa palveluntuottaja toimittaa ne laboratorioon. SUEK käyttää lähettämiseen ainoastaan omia kuljetusmateriaalejaan/-laukkujaan. SUEKilla tulee olla mahdollisuus kuljetuksen online-seurantaan lähetystunnuksen avulla verkossa tai mobiilisovelluksella. Peruskuljetuspalvelua (lähetyksen noutoa) ei erikseen tilata, vaan SUEKin edustaja toimittaa lähetyksen valitsemaansa noutopisteeseen (lähetyspisteeseen). Lähetyspisteet ja niiden kappalemäärät per paikkakunta on esitetty tarjouspyynnössä. Palveluntuottaja noutaa lähetyksen noutopisteestä ja kuljettaa sen laboratorioon. Lisäksi SUEKilla tulee olla myös mahdollisuus tilata nouto suoraan ovelle. Tässä tapauksessa SUEKin edustaja tilaa noudon ovelle etukäteen sovituksi ajankohdaksi. Peruskuljetuksen tulee olla perillä laboratoriossa lähtökohtaisesti seuraavana arkipäivänä klo 8.00–13.45 välisenä aikana, mikäli lähetys on viety noutopisteeseen palveluntuottajan kanssa ennalta sovittuun kellonaikaan (esim. klo 14.00 tai 16.30, voi vaihdella paikkakunnasta riippuen) mennessä. Palveluntuottajalla on mahdollisuus pidempään toimitusaikaan, mikäli kuljetusmatka Helsingissä sijaitsevaan laboratorioon on yli viisisataa (500) kilometriä. Edellä mainitussa tapauksessa toimitusaika ei kuitenkaan saa olla yli kahta (2) arkipäivää. Mikäli lähetys on jätetty noutopisteen aikataulun rajoissa (ts. ennen ko. pisteen viimeistä jättöaikaa), on lähetys toimitettava Helsingin Laboratorioon 1 - 2 arkipäivän sisällä., Osa-alue 2 Erikoiskuljetuspalvelut Osa-alue 2 (Erikoiskuljetuspalvelut) koskee dopingnäytteiden (virtsa- ja verinäytteiden) kuljettamista laboratorioon. Palveluntuottajan tulee antaa tarjous myös erikoiskuljetuspalveluista ulkomaille siten, kuin tarjouspyynnössä on tarkemmin määritelty. Erikoiskuljetuspalveluihin kohdistuu nimensä mukaisesti peruskuljetuspalveluista poikkeavia erityisjärjestelyjä. Erityisjärjestelyt voivat liittyä esimerkiksi o kuljetuksen normaalista poikkeavaan ajankohtaan; o lähetyspaikkaan; o kriittiseen kuljetusaikatauluun; tai o kaikkiin edellä mainittuihin tekijöihin. SUEK tilaa erikoiskuljetuspalvelut palveluntuottajalta etukäteen puhelimitse tai sähköpostilla. Palveluntuottaja toimittaa tilauksesta tilausvahvistuksen sähköpostilla tai sähköisen järjestelmänsä kautta. Palveluntuottajan tulee vastata puhelimitse tehtyyn palvelupyyntöön kuudenkymmenen (60) minuutin kuluessa, mikäli palvelupyyntö on tehty klo 8.00–16.00 välisenä aikana. Sähköpostitse tehtyyn palvelupyyntöön tulee vastata saman päivän aikana, mikäli palvelupyyntö on tehty klo 8–16 välisenä aikana. Palveluntuottaja sitoutuu suorittamaan erikoiskuljetuspalvelut sovitusti lyhyelläkin varoitusajalla siten, että palveluntuottajan on noudettava lähetys viimeistään kahdentoista (12) tunnin kuluttua siitä, kun SUEK on tehnyt palvelupyynnön sovitulla tavalla palveluntuottajan 24/7 päivystykseen. SUEKilla on aina (24/7) oikeus peruuttaa erikoiskuljetus ennen ennalta sovittua lähetyksen noutoaikaa ilmoittamalla asiasta viipymättä palveluntuottajalle. SUEK ei maksa peruuntuneesta erikoiskuljetuksesta. Palveluntuottajalla on kuitenkin oikeus veloittaa tosiasialliset ja kohtuulliset kustannukset, joita palvelun tuottamisen mahdollisesta aloittamisesta on ehtinyt jo syntyä ennen peruutusta. SUEKin tämänhetkisen arvion mukaan erikoiskuljetuspalveluihin sisältyviä lähetyksiä tulee 0-8 kappaletta kuukaudessa siten, että yhden lähetyksen paino on noin 2-8 kg. SUEK ei kuitenkaan ole sidottu mihinkään tilausmääriin, vaan hyödyntää kuljetuspalveluita tosiasiallisen tarpeensa mukaan. Erikoiskuljetuspalvelu toteutetaan ns. ovelta ovelle kuriiripalveluna, eli palveluntuottaja noutaa lähetyksen suoraan SUEKin edustajalta etukäteen sovitusta paikasta sovittuna aikana. SUEK huolehtii itse näytteiden pakkaamisesta SUEKin omiin sinetöityihin kuljetuslaukkuihin, joissa palveluntuottaja toimittaa ne laboratorioon. SUEK käyttää lähettämiseen ainoastaan omia kuljetusmateriaalejaan/-laukkujaan. SUEKilla tulee olla mahdollisuus kuljetuksen online-seurantaan lähetystunnuksen avulla verkossa tai mobiilisovelluksella. Erikoiskuljetuspalvelun hintaan sisältyy palveluntuottajan tarjoama puhelinpäivystyspalvelu (24/7, vuoden jokaisena päivänä) suomen tai englannin kielellä.,

title: Greece – Diesel fuel – Προμήθεια καυσίμων του Δήμου Νότιας Κέρκυρας
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η προμήθεια υγρού καυσίμου (πετρέλαιο κίνησης diesel, βενζίνη αμόλυβδη και πετρέλαιο θέρμανσης) και πρόσθετου τύπου AdBlue (διάλυμα ουρίας), προκειμένου ο Δήμος Νότιας Κέρκυρας να καλύψει τις ανάγκες θέρμανσης των σχολικών κτιρίων και παιδικών/βρεφονηπιακών σταθμών που βρίσκονται εντός των διοικητικών ορίων του, καθώς και τις ανάγκες κίνησης των οχημάτων και μηχανημάτων έργου των υπηρεσιών του Δήμου, όπως επίσης και για την λειτουργία τωνδιαφόρων εργαλείων με κινητήρες εσωτερικής καύσης (χορτοκοπτικά, πριόνια κ.λπ.) τα οποία έχουν στην διάθεσή τους οι υπηρεσίες του Δήμου, είναι απαραίτητη η προμήθεια πετρελαίου θέρμανσης, πετρελαίου κίνησης, αμόλυβδης βενζίνης καθώς και υδατικού διαλύματος ουρίας (τύπου AdBlue) για τις ανάγκες των υπηρεσιακών οχημάτων, που είναι εφοδιασμένα με σύστημα επεξεργασίας καυσαερίων Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR). Προσφορές υποβάλλονται και για τα τέσσερα υπό προμήθεια είδη. Προσφορά οικονομικού φορέα η οποία δεν θα αφορά και τα τέσσερα υπό προμήθεια είδη (καύσιμα και πρόσθετο AdBlue) θα απορρίπτεται ως απαράδεκτη. Η αναθέτουσα αρχή προβαίνει στη συγκεκριμένη ανάθεση χωρίς διαχωρισμό σε τμήματα, καθώς η προμήθεια αφορά το σύνολο των απαιτούμενων καυσίμων και του πρόσθετου AdBlue για την κάλυψη των αναγκών του Δήμου Νότιας Κέρκυρας κατά τα έτη 2027–2028. Η προσφορά πρέπει να περιλαμβάνει και τα τέσσερα είδη, σύμφωνα με τους όρους της παρούσας διακήρυξης και της σχετικής μελέτης

title: Pfungen, Buckstrasse - Strassensanierung mit Werkleitungen
description:
Im Sinne der Werterhaltung ist die Sanierung der Buckstrasse im Innerortsabschnitt vorgesehen. Im Zuge dieser strassenbaulichen Massnahme wird die öffentliche Beleuchtung normgerecht sowie entsprechend den aktuellen Standards angepasst. Die Infrastrukturen der Gas- und Wasserversorgung wurden bereits erneuert; diesbezügliche Sanierungsmassnahmen sind nicht erforderlich. Das bestehende Konzept der Abwasser- und Entwässerungsanlagen bleibt grundsätzlich unverändert. Gemäss den Vorgaben im Rahmen der GEP-Erarbeitung wird im unteren und mittleren Abschnitt auf einer Länge von rund 250m die Mischabwasserleitung ersetzt. In diesem Zusammenhang erfolgen Kalibererweiterungen zur Behebung hydraulischer Überlastungen. Die Anlagen der Strassenentwässerung werden neu erstellt, während die in der Fahrbahn und im Gehweg längs verlaufende Sickerleitung bestehen bleibt.

Mit der Einführung einer Tempo-30 Zone wird der Strassenraum verkehrsberuhigt umgestaltet und an das neue Temporegime angepasst. Die hierfür vorgesehenen baulichen Massnahmen wurden im Verfahren nach Strassengesetz (StrG) aufgelegt, rechtskräftig festgesetzt und sind Bestandteil des vorliegenden Strassenprojekts.

title: Itäkeskuksen joukkoliikenneterminaalin arkkitehtuurikilpailu
description: Itäkeskuksen joukkoliikenneterminaalin arkkitehtuurikilpailu Pääkaupunkiseudun Kaupunkiliikenne Oy julkaisee arkkitehtuurikilpailua koskevan ilmoituksen Itäkeskuksen joukkoliikenneterminaalin arkkitehtisuunnittelusta Helsingin Joukkoliikenneinfra Oy:n ja Helsingin kaupungin liikenneliikelaitoksen (HKL) puolesta. Korttelialueella on tällä hetkellä Itäkeskuksen metroaseman sisäänkäynti, kaksi pysäköintilaitosta ja näiden kansitasolla bussiterminaali. Helsingin kaupunkistrategian 2025-2029 tavoitteiden mukaisesti Itäkeskusta kehitetään kunnianhimoisesti. Itäkeskuksen joukkoliikenneterminaalin uudistuksessa tavoitteena on luoda sujuvat vaihtoyhteydet eri liikennevälineiden välillä. Joukkoliikenneterminaalin suunnittelussa tavoitellaan viihtyisää, turvallista ja saavutettavaa kokonaisuutta. Hyvällä suunnittelulla halutaan varmistaa, että liikennevälineestä toiseen siirtyminen on helppoa ja sujuvaa ja tarpeelliset palvelut ovat lähellä. Uudistuksen myötä pikaraitiotie PR15 päätepysäkki sijoitetaan osaksi joukkoliikenneterminaalikorttelia. Kilpailun tavoitteena on luoda kaupunkikuvallisesti kiinnostavaa ja alueelle vahvaa identiteettiä luovaa ratkaisua. Kilpailu järjestetään yhteistyössä Helsingin kaupungin ja Suomen arkkitehtiliitto SAFA:n kanssa, liiton yleisesti käyttämien kilpailusääntöjen mukaisesti. Tarkemmat tiedot kilpailuohjelmasta, kilpailun verkkosivuilta. https://cc.tietoa.fi/c/itis-jlt Helsingin kaupungin liikenneliikelaitos ja Helsingin Joukkoliikenneinfra Oy tilaavat arkkitehtuurikilpailun voittaneelta taholta hankkeen pää- ja arkkitehtisuunnittelun, mikäli seuraavat edellytykset täyttyvät: - kilpailun voittajalla, tulevalla sopimuskumppanilla on tekijänoikeudet suunnitelmaan - kilpailun voittaja nimeää vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät kaksi henkilöä eli pääsuunnittelijan ja vastuullisen arkkitehtisuunnittelijan, voittaja voi myös itse toimia toisessa em. rooleista - tilaajat ja kilpailun voittaja pääsevät neuvotteluissa yhteisymmärrykseen sopimusehdoista ja suunnittelupalkkiosta (kattohinta ja tuntihinnat). Tehtävä käsittää seuraavien tehtäväluetteloiden mukaiset tehtävät: Hankesuunnittelu tehtäväluetteloiden kohdat B- D, Yleissuunnitelmat ja toteutuksen suunnittelu tehtäväluetteloiden kohdat E-G, Rakentamisen aikaiset ja takuuajan tehtävät tehtäväluetteloiden kohdat H-K. Tehtävä sisältää työturvallisuuslain mukaiset suunnittelijan velvoitteet sekä rakennustyön turvallisuutta koskevan asetuksen VNa 205/2009, 7§ mukaiset velvoitteet. Pääsuunnittelijaa ja vastuullista arkkitehtisuunnittelijaa koskevat vähimmäisvaatimukset: 1) Suunnittelijoilla tulee olla rakentamislain mukainen, oman alansa pätevyystodistus erittäin vaativalta tasolta. 2) Nimettävillä suunnittelijoilla tulee olla kokemusta vastaavan tyyppisestä ja laajuisesta hankkeesta hankkeen eri vaiheissa esimerkiksi matkustajaterminaalin, rautatieaseman, lentokenttäterminaalin, kauppakeskuksen tms. suunnittelusta, jossa on huomioitu suurien asiakas-, matkustaja- tai kävijämäärien hallinta. Kohteen erityislaatuisuuden vuoksi voidaan huomioida myös yli viisi (5) vuotta sitten valmistunut hanke. 3) Suunnittelijoilla tulee olla vähintään hyvä suullinen ja kirjallinen suomen kielen taito. Neuvottelut toimeksiantosopimuksesta Neuvottelut aloitetaan viimeistään kolmen (3) viikon kuluttua kilpailun ratkaisemisesta, jolloin neuvotteluihin kutsutun tulee neuvottelujen alkaessa esittää tilaajille pääsuunnittelijan ja vastuullisen arkkitehtisuunnittelijan rooleihin ehdotetut, vähimmäisvaatimukset (1-3) täyttävät henkilöt hyväksyttäväksi. Neuvottelut käydään suomen kielellä ja sopimus laaditaan suomen kielisenä. Voittajan kanssa käydään neuvottelut kolmen (3) kuukauden aikana suunnittelukilpailun voittajan valinnan jälkeen. Tavoitteena tässä ajassa on saada molempien osapuolten hyväksymä näkemys sopimuksen ehdoista ja suunnittelupalkkiosta. Neuvottelujen jälkeen tilaajat tekevät hankintapäätökset toimeksiannosta. Toimeksiantosopimus laaditaan RT 80420 -sopimuspohjaan. Tilaaja laatii osapuolten väliseen neuvotteluun sopimusluonnoksen ja sen ehdot sekä sopimuksen liitteet. Sopimukseen liitetään mm. arkkitehtisuunnittelun tehtäväluettelo ARK18:n (RT 10-103253) ja pääsuunnittelun tehtäväluettelo PS18:n (RT 10–103254) soveltuvin osin sekä tietosuoja- ja salassapitoliite. Toimeksiannossa noudatetaan KSE 2013 ehtoja soveltuvin osin, ks. tilaajien esittämät liitteessä poikkeamat KSE 2013 ehdoista. Tilaajat varaavat mahdollisuuden tarkentaa ja täydentää poikkeamia koskevaa listausta tulevaan sopimusneuvotteluun. Tarvittavat kokoukset hankkeen eri vaiheissa sisältyvät tulevaan toimeksiantoon. Kokoukset täsmennetään tehtäväluettelojen mukaisesti sopimusneuvotteluvaiheessa. Hankkeessa käytetään projektipankkia, johon kaikki tuotetut dokumentit tallennetaan projektipankissa olevan ohjeistuksen mukaisesti. Hanke suunnitellaan tietomallipohjaisesti. Joukkoliikenneterminaalihankkeen edistäminen on ehdollinen sille, että tilaajat saavat tarvittavat päätökset hankkeen edistämiseen.,

title: Liminganlahden lintornit ja p-alue
description: Liminganlahden lintornit ja p-alue Liminganlahden Ystävät Ry:llä on käynnissä Pohjois-Suopmen elinvoimakeskuksen / Maaseuturahaston rahoittama Liminganlahden muuttajat -hanke. Hankinta tehdään osana tätä hanketta. Liminganlahden luontokeskuksen alueelle rakennetaan uusi parkkialue, olemassa oleva vanha lintutorni puretaan pois, lintutornille menevä polku parannetaan, sekä rakennetaan uudet näköalatorni sekä lintutorni. Hankinta on tarkemmin kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Tarjoajan tulee tutustua tarjouspyyntöön ja sen liitteisiin. Urakoitsijan tulee suorittaa kaikki ne työt ja niihin liittyvät hankinnat, jotka asiakirjojen mukaisen työsuorituksen valmiiksi saattaminen edellyttää ja joista ei nimenomaan asiakirjoissa mainita, etteivät ne kuulu urakoitsijan suoritusvelvollisuuteen. Urakka on kokonaisurakka urakka-asiakirjoissa ilmoitetuille työmäärille. Kokonaishinnan määrittämiseksi urakoitsijan tulee laskea kaikki tarvitsemansa työ- ja materiaalimäärät. Kokonaishinnan tulee perustua suunnitelmista ja muista urakka-asiakirjoista ilmeneviin määriin. Urakkakohteen työt voidaan aloittaa, kun urakoitsijan valintaa koskeva päätös on lainvoimainen ja urakkasopimus on allekirjoitettu sekä rakennusajan vakuudet on toimitettu tilaajille. Urakoitsijan tulee toimittaa urakan yleisaikataulu tilaajalle ennen aloituskokousta. Urakan on oltava valmiina kaikkine töineen ja luovutusaineistoineen viimeistään 28.6.2027. Kaikki paalutukset ja valut on oltava valmiina 15.3.2027 mennessä. Hankinnasta solmitaan urakkasopimus yhden (1) urakoitsijan (pääurakoitsija) kanssa. Pääurakoitsija voi antaa osan töistä tilaajalla hyväksytettäville aliurakoitsijoille. Hankintaan sovelletaan YSE98-sopimusehtoja. Hankinnan arvioidaan ylittävän hankintalain 25 § kynnysarvon.,

title: Packing and Crating
description: 1. The United States Air Forces in Europe and Africa (USAFE-AFAFRICA) requires packing and crating services across the Kaiserslautern Military Community, Spangdahlem Air Base, and Lajes Field, Azores, Portugal areas. These services will include, but are not limited to, furnishment of all personnel, equipment, facilities, supplies, services, and materials, except as specified, for the preparation of the personal property (including servicing of appliances) of personnel for shipment, drayage and/or storage and related services through the Direct Procurement Method (DPM). 2. The Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC) 764th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (ESS) provides contracting support to USAFE-AFAFRICA. 764 ESS is seeking industry feedback and to ascertain industry�s capability in performing the scope of work as detailed in the Performance Work Statement. 3. This Request for Information (RFI) is for Market Research purposes only and shall not be considered as an invitation to bid, request for quotation, request for proposal, or as an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. AFICC 764 ESS is not seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals as a result of this RFI. No contract awards will be made from this notice, and no solicitation is available at this time. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses to this announcement or the Government use of such information. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. 4. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Companies may be contacted if we need further information to fully understand the marketplace. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal (RFP). 5. Comments and responses are due no later than 3:00 PM local Ramstein, Germany time on 18 December 2026. Please submit your responses to the Government points of contact indicated below: Contracting Officer: Zachary Laurenz, zachary.laurenz.1@us.af.mil Program Manager: Kayla Amie, kayla.amie@us.af.mil

title: Q702--North Kansas City OPC Initial Outfitting Transition Activation Contract
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) November 4, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the North Kansas OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for the North Kansas Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 38-months. This project proposes to lease an approximately 102,736 NUSF replacement and expanded Outpatient Clinic in the vicinity of Kansas City, MO, including 700 parking spaces. The new facility allows for decompression of the Kansas City VAMC. The lease would allow VA to enhance outpatient services by closing space gaps identified in the SCIP process. The new lease would expand the current Primary Care space, allowing for the full implementation of the PACT model of care delivery, improving operational efficiencies and the Veteran experience. The newly leased right-sized, state-of-the-art, energy-efficient health care facility would provide Primary Care, Mental Health, Specialty Care, Outpatient Surgery and Ancillary services to Veterans in the Kansas City area. The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 19 November 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 18 December 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson6@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson6@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Restauration de la libre circulation des poissons / Réfection des centrales électriques / Renouvellement de la concession, phases SIA 32 à 53
description:
L'objectif principal du projet est de garantir, à partir de 2030 environ, une production d'énergie renouvelable issue de l'hydroélectricité qui soit durable à long terme et économiquement viable. Cela comprend les objectifs partiels suivants :

  1. La concession pour l'exploitation de l'énergie hydraulique des centrales d'Obertöss et de Niedertöss est garantie pour au moins 40 ans supplémentaires, dans des conditions-cadres économiquement viables. En outre, il doit être possible de constituer une provision pour le démantèlement des installations à l’expiration de la concession.
  2. Les exigences légales en matière de restauration de la libre circulation des poissons seront respectées, en garantissant la prise en charge intégrale des coûts par la Confédération.
  3. La protection des monuments historiques sera réglementée de manière contraignante et à long terme dans le cadre des objectifs partiels 1) et 2). Un développement et une modernisation modérés des installations des centrales électriques pendant la durée de la concession doivent être garantis.

L’objectif intermédiaire consiste à créer, par le biais de travaux de planification jusqu’à la demande de permis de construire ou de concession incluse, un cadre juridique contraignant, de sorte que la remise en état et la rénovation puissent ensuite être mises en œuvre de manière autonome ou que les installations, y compris le projet associé approuvé en toute sécurité juridique, puissent être vendues. C’est pourquoi les phases 41 à 53, conformément à la norme SIA 112, ne font l’objet d’un appel d’offres qu’à titre facultatif.

title: Germany – Repair and maintenance services of security and defence materials – BG_1714_EU/26 - Werksinstandsetzung von verschiedenen Baugruppen des Systems TPz 1 Fuchs
description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von verschiedenen Baugruppen des Systems TPz 1 Fuchs. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet am 31.12.2030. Des Weiteren behält sich der Auftraggeber eine optionale Verlängerung der Rahmenvereinbarung bis zum 31.12.2033 vor. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

description: Please carefully read and complete the entire solicitation document. Description: This is a solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 67100PR270000152 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ), request for monthly preventive maintenance for 219 Government-owned fitness equipment items in the Building 269 gymnasium. This acquisition is set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 Effective Date 03/13/2026. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 811490. with a small business size standard of $9.0M. Product Service Code is J078. This requirement is a recompete of a previously awarded contract. For informational purposes, offerors may view prior award information on USAspending.gov using Award ID 70Z04322PCMAY0011. Submission of offers. Submit signed and dated offers to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified in this solicitation. As a minimum, offers shall include� (1) The solicitation number. (2) The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror. (3) The Offeror�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) (4) Information necessary to evaluate the factors contained in the provision at 52.212-2 (5) Responses to provisions that require Offeror completion of information, representations, and certifications (other than those collected via the System for Award Management (SAM)); and (6) A statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments. Period for acceptance of offers. The Offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation. 52.237-1 Site Visit (Apr 1984) Ensuring accurate bid submissions is crucial to the success of our project. Therefore, we strongly encourage all bidders to conduct a thorough site visit to verify quantities before finalizing their bids. It is expected that offerors or quoters inspect the site where the work will be performed to better understand the scope of the project. To facilitate this process, an organized site visit has been scheduled for Wednesday December 9, 2026, at 9:30 am est. Participants are requested to assemble at TRACEN CAPE MAY 1 Munro Ave, Cape May, NJ 08204. Please note that all visitors must provide the following information prior to scheduling a site visit: full legal name, date of birth, contact number, email address, Real Id Driver�s License, registration of vehicle and proof of insurance. No personnel with felony convictions are permitted to access Coast Guard facilities under any circumstance. All vendors interested in attending the site visit must submit a site-visit request through the secure form at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Zh9ErQgWwu by Tuesday December 8, 2026, at 11:00 am est. with the following information: 1: Company Name 2. Company Phone 3: Visitor Name 4: Last 4 of SSN: 5: Date of Birth: 6: Place of Birth: 7: Real Id Driver�s License Number: The U.S. Coast Guard Training Center Cape May is seeking to purchase monthly preventive maintenance services for 219 Government-owned fitness equipment items located in the Building 269 gymnasium. Offerors shall insert a single monthly unit price and extended amount for each CLIN. The monthly unit price may differ by performance period. Extended amount equals the monthly unit price multiplied by 12. The Government will evaluate pricing in accordance with the solicitation. Base Period April 1, 2027 � March 31, 2028: Task One - Monthly preventive maintenance for 219 equipment items and associated monthly report and service log. Option Period One April 1, 2028 � March 31, 2029: Task One - Monthly preventive maintenance for 219 equipment items and associated monthly report and service log. Option Period Two April 1, 2029 � March 31, 2030: Task One - Monthly preventive maintenance for 219 equipment items and associated monthly report and service log. Option Period Three April 1, 2030 � March 31, 2031: Task One - Monthly preventive maintenance for 219 equipment items and associated monthly report and service log. Option Period Four April 1, 2031 � March 31, 2032: Task One - Monthly preventive maintenance for 219 equipment items and associated monthly report and service log. Each CLIN is an FFP, severable monthly service unit. The unit price shall include all labor, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, reporting, and other costs necessary to perform the corresponding monthly preventive-maintenance service described in the SOW. Offerors are required to provide prices for all items/CLINs. A zero-dollar figure ($0.00) unit price means the offeror shall provide the service/supply at no charge to the Government. Unit prices left blank or annotated with something other than a dollar figure will be considered unacceptable. Reference Attached Statement of Work in Solicitation 67100PR270000152. Place of Performance: U.S. Coast Guard Training Center (TRACEN) Cape May operates a gymnasium in Building 269 at 1 Munro Avenue, Cape May, New Jersey 08204. Basis for Award: Quotations will be evaluated in an efficient and minimally burdensome manner. The Government will evaluate quotations using the following factors: Technical Capability Price The Government will make award to the Offeror that submits the lowest-priced quotation rated Technically Acceptable. Technical Capability: The Government will evaluate whether the Offeror demonstrates the capability to perform all requirements in the Statement of Work (SOW). To be rated Technically Acceptable, the quotation must demonstrate all of the following: Relevant Experience. The Offeror has performed at least two contracts or subcontracts within the past three years for preventive maintenance of comparable mixed commercial fitness equipment. Comparable experience may include preventive maintenance of motorized cardio equipment, non-motorized cardio equipment, strength equipment, cable equipment, or similar commercial fitness equipment. The Government will not require the prior work to involve an identical quantity of equipment or the same equipment brands identified in the SOW. Maintenance Approach. The Offeror provides a clear approach for completing monthly preventive maintenance for all 219 equipment items identified in the SOW. The approach must address the required inspections, cleaning, lubrication, diagnostic checks, calibration, and hardware checks, as applicable to the equipment type and original equipment manufacturer procedures. Personnel, Tools, and Procedures. The Offeror confirms it will provide qualified personnel, supervision, tools, test equipment, transportation, and other resources necessary to perform the required services. The Offeror must also confirm it will use applicable original equipment manufacturer procedures or accepted commercial industry practices when original equipment manufacturer procedures are not available. Scheduling, Safety, and Reporting. The Offeror confirms it can meet the SOW requirements for scheduling monthly visits, identifying and tagging unsafe or non-operational equipment, notifying the Government Technical Representative (GTR), and submitting the Monthly Preventive Maintenance Report and Service Log within the required timeframe. Monthly Report and Service Log. The Offeror provides a sample report/service log or a description of the proposed report

title: Belgium – Test and evaluation – Framework service contract for defence testing and evaluation campaigns and other operational experimentation activities
description: This procurement establishes a four-year framework contract for the provision of support services for the BraveTech EU Testing and Evaluation Campaigns and other defence innovation and experimentation activities conducted by EDA under CEDI.BraveTech EU is an initiative funded by the European Union under the European Defence Fund (EDF) and implemented by the European Defence Agency under indirect management. However, this procurement is not limited to BraveTech EU. It may also be used to order similar services in support of other EDA defence innovation and operational experimentation activities conducted under the Centre for European Defence Innovation (CEDI), which may be funded from other sources. BraveTech EU comprises eight (8) cycles with sixteen (16) campaigns (Phase 1 and Phase 2) in total. Within the DefTech Forges (Phase 1), companies presenting solutions at TRL 4 and above, addressing the most urgent defence challenges defined by the EU Member States, Norway and Ukraine, received monetary prizes. Building on Phase 1 DefTech Forges, Phase 2 comprises sixteen (16) Testing and Evaluation Campaigns, in which Phase 1 pre-selected companies test and refine their solutions under operational conditions. The two campaigns of the first cycle (Phase 2-TEC 1 and TEC 2) are delivered directly by EDA and are outside the scope of this framework contract. Consequently, cycle two to cycle eight (cycles 2-8) with fourteen (14) campaigns fall within the scope of this framework contract. The framework contract is concluded for a duration of four (4) years, and the estimated maximum value is EUR 40 000 000. The activities under BraveTech EU Phase 2 shall be completed by 31 December 2028 and the estimated maximum value is approximately 13 000 000 EUR. For this procedure, m maximum of five (5) best ranked candidates meeting the selection criteria and the scoring thresholds will be invited to submit a tender in Step 2. Where fewer than five (5) candidates meet those requirements, EDA may continue the procedure by inviting only the candidates that satisfy them to submit a tender.

title: FEMA Request for Information - Direct Housing Modernization Capabilities
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is for Market Research purposes ONLY. Please read the notice and attachment in full. Please limit questions to those directly related to the posted RFI Notice and the information requested therein. Questions submitted in response to this RFI Notice may not receive a response. Questions outside the scope of this notice, including matters unrelated to the stated capability requirements, will not receive a response. The Government will consider only questions that are directly relevant to the notice and the requested capability information. If responses are provided, relevant questions and Government responses, if any, will be posted to Sam.gov ONLY after the Request for Information Notice has closed. RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit Questions and RFI responses electronically to the Contracting Officer, at Rachel.Woods@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Time (ET), December 18, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c). This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response to this request. All information contained in this RFI is preliminary and is subject to change if, and when, a solicitation is issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a competitive solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this RFI, or future solicitations. The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Office of Direct Housing Operations, is conducting market research to identify and seek capabilities from industry in five primary functional areas: Automated Real Estate Aggregation and Vacancy Sourcing - Automated discovery and ingestion of residential rental property listings via Multiple Listing Services (MLS), property management software APIs, commercial rental boards, and direct landlord entry portals. - Real-time vacancy validation to prevent matching against obsolete or unavailable listings. - Rapid geo-fencing within disaster-declared zones and surrounding reasonable-commute perimeters. Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Matching - Multi-constraint matching algorithms that pair applicant household profiles with available properties in seconds. - Multi-point geospatial proximity optimization factoring in school district retention, work commutes, medical/provider travel distance, and essential services. - Household composition sizing aligned with HUD Housing Quality Standards (HQS) and FEMA occupancy guidelines. Automated Physical Accessibility Verification - Algorithmic filtering and computer vision inspection tools capable of evaluating floor plans, entry photos, and property specifications against UFAS and ADA physical accessibility standards. - Rapid identification of barrier-free environments, ramps, ground-floor units, grab bars, and wheelchair-accessible kitchens and bathrooms. Landlord Engagement and Leasing Workflow Automation - Automated outreach tools and self-service portals for landlords to submit properties, accept lease terms, and coordinate inspections. - Integration with standard government lease templates and automated electronic signature workflows. Secure Federal Architecture - Enterprise data security architecture compliant with the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) at the Moderate impact baseline. - FedRAMP-authorized cloud hosting (or capability to achieve FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization). - Strict data protection for Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) belonging to disaster survivors. title: FEMA Request for Information - Direct Housing Modernization Capabilities
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c). This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response to this request. All information contained in this RFI is preliminary and is subject to change if, and when, a solicitation is issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a competitive solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this RFI, or future solicitations. The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Office of Direct Housing Operations, is conducting market research to identify and seek capabilities from industry in five primary functional areas: Automated Real Estate Aggregation and Vacancy Sourcing - Automated discovery and ingestion of residential rental property listings via Multiple Listing Services (MLS), property management software APIs, commercial rental boards, and direct landlord entry portals. - Real-time vacancy validation to prevent matching against obsolete or unavailable listings. - Rapid geo-fencing within disaster-declared zones and surrounding reasonable-commute perimeters. Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Matching - Multi-constraint matching algorithms that pair applicant household profiles with available properties in seconds. - Multi-point geospatial proximity optimization factoring in school district retention, work commutes, medical/provider travel distance, and essential services. - Household composition sizing aligned with HUD Housing Quality Standards (HQS) and FEMA occupancy guidelines. Automated Physical Accessibility Verification - Algorithmic filtering and computer vision inspection tools capable of evaluating floor plans, entry photos, and property specifications against UFAS and ADA physical accessibility standards. - Rapid identification of barrier-free environments, ramps, ground-floor units, grab bars, and wheelchair-accessible kitchens and bathrooms. Landlord Engagement and Leasing Workflow Automation - Automated outreach tools and self-service portals for landlords to submit properties, accept lease terms, and coordinate inspections. - Integration with standard government lease templates and automated electronic signature workflows. Secure Federal Architecture - Enterprise data security architecture compliant with the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) at the Moderate impact baseline. - FedRAMP-authorized cloud hosting (or capability to achieve FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization). - Strict data protection for Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) belonging to disaster survivors. NAICS CODE: 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) / 531210 (Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers) PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): X1FA, Lease/Rental of Family Housing Facilities ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: TBD RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit Questions and RFI responses electronically to the Contracting Officer, at Rachel.Woods@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Time (ET), December 18, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted. Please see the attachment for further instructions and information.

description: NTRODUCTION In support of the U.S. Army, 99th Readiness Division, the US Army Contracting Command Rock Island � Fort Dix is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for Custodial Services. The intention is to procure these services on a competitive basis. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and only one award MAY be made. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. PLACE(S) OF PERFORMANCE MAJ Holleder USARC 515 Old Ridge Road, Webster NY 14580-1789 DISCLAIMER �THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)� TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT.� REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Contractor shall provide custodial services in support of the U.S Army, 99th Readiness Division. Further detail is provided in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Custodial Floor Plan attached to this announcement. Attachment(s): NY070 Webster PWS - Custodial - FY27 Version 3 NY070_CUST_JUL2026_UNCLASSIFIED If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these custodial services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The Government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to: 1) provide services consistent, in scope and scale, with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; and 2) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. The Product Service Code is S201 Housekeeping- Custodial Janitorial. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. The deadline for response to this request is no later than 12:00 AM, EST, 18 December 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be e-mailed to Alyssa Hampton, Contract Specialist, alyssa.l.hampton2.civ@army.mil. This documentation must address at a minimum the following items: 1.) What type of work has your company performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement? 2.) Can or has your company managed a task of this nature? If so, please provide details. 3.) Can or has your company managed a team of subcontractors before? If so, provide details. 4.) What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensure capability to perform the tasks? 5.) Please note that under a Small-Business Set-Aside, in accordance with FAR 52.219-14, the small business prime must perform at least 50% of the work themselves in terms of the cost of performance. Provide an explanation of your company�s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS for the base period as well as the option periods. 6.) Provide a statement including current small/large business status and company profile to CAGE, DUNS and SAM Unique Identity. 7.) Respondents to this notice also must indicate whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Women-Owned, HUBZone, or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. The estimated period of performance consists of base year plus 4, 12-months. Specifics regarding the number of option periods will be provided in the solicitation. The contract type is anticipated to be firm-fixed priced. The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking that would be accomplished by labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act or a collective bargaining agreement. Upon evaluation of the capability statements, if it is determined that this requirement will be an unrestricted competition, the Government intends to evaluate the Small-Business responses and conduct further market research to identify a subcontracting goal. Your response to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted to the Contract Specialist, Alyssa Hampton, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF), via email alyssa.l.hampton2.civ@army.mil. All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted to the contract specialist identified above. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL SERVICES Solicitation Number: 20150PR270000020 Project Title: USCG Air Station Clearwater Carpet Replacement � FACENG and Supply Offices Issuing Agency: United States Coast Guard (USCG) � Base Miami Beach (Procurement & Contracting) Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside Applicable NAICS Code: 238330 � Flooring Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Acquisition Authority: FAR Subpart 12.6 (Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items), FAR Part 13 (Simplified Acquisition Procedures), and FAR Part 15 Performance Location: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater, 15100 Rescue Way, Clearwater, FL 33762 1. General Notice & Acquisition Overview This document constitutes a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services and minor facility improvements prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Sole Solicitation: This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Set-Aside: This solicitation is advertised as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. Offers received from entities other than small business concerns under NAICS code 238330 will not be considered. Basis of Award: Award will be made using simplified acquisition procedures to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all solicitation requirements and represents the Best Value to the Government, considering technical capability/approach, past performance, and price. 2. Schedule of Supplies / Services & Pricing The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, disposal, and incidental services necessary to complete the carpet replacement project as specified in the Statement of Work. Offerors are responsible for field-verifying all measurements during the pre-quote site visit prior to submitting their quote. 3. Site Visit Information A formal site visit has been scheduled for prospective offerors to inspect the existing site conditions, verify carpet and cove base dimensions, evaluate access routes, and inspect furniture configurations. Date & Time: Thursday, December 10, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST Location: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater 15100 Rescue Way, Clearwater, FL 33762 Primary COR: CWO Joe Calderon � Jose.A.Calderon@uscg.mil | Phone: (727) 423-7586 Alternate POC: LCDR Scott Kellerman � scott.n.kellerman@uscg.mil | Phone: (571) 499-0711 Required Security Submission for Site Visit: Real ID-compliant Driver�s License Number and State of Issuance Site Access Rules: Only U.S. citizens and permanent resident aliens are allowed onboard Air Station Clearwater. Attendees must present valid government photo identification at the front gate. Vehicles and equipment are subject to inspection at all times. 4. Statement of Work (SOW) � Project 33643384 4.1 Scope of Work Summary The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, materials, delivery, furniture moving, carpet and cove base removal, surface preparation, installation, cleanup, and disposal for the complete replacement of existing carpet and cove base throughout designated administrative areas within the FACENG and Supply building. All work must comply with the Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI) 104 Standard for Installation of Commercial Carpet, manufacturer written instructions, and applicable federal, state, and local standards. 4.2 Included Areas and Approximate Takeoffs FACENG and Conference Areas: Rooms 115, 116, 119, 122, former Room 114 suite (conference room, adjoining office, and internal passages): approximately 1,150 sq. ft. Supply Office Areas: Rooms 102, 103, 104, 107, 108, 109, and 110: approximately 1,670 sq. ft. Combined Planning Takeoff: Approximately 2,820 square feet of carpet tile and 775 linear feet of cove base. Excluded Areas: Hard-floor supply warehouse, public corridors/vestibules, main lobby, restrooms, mechanical rooms, and shop floors. Period of Performance: Total period of performance shall be forty-five (45) calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). Schedule Submission: The Contractor shall provide a phased, room-by-room work schedule outlining start dates, sequence, weekend milestones, and completion 4.4 Technical Requirements & Material Specifications 1. Carpet Tile: Commercial-grade, heavy/severe-traffic-rated modular carpet tiles equal to or exceeding existing durability and aesthetic standards. Materials must originate from consistent production runs/dye lots within each contiguous area. 2. Cove Base: Commercial resilient cove base matching existing height (minimum nominal height of 4 inches). 3. Submittals & Approval: Prior to material ordering, the Contractor must submit product technical data, adhesive specifications, color lines, transition details, and manufacturer warranty certificates to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). The COR will select final colors and patterns. 4. Subfloor Preparation: Remove old adhesive residue, perform mechanical scraping, patch cracks/depressions, and verify moisture and pH levels per manufacturer criteria before laying tile. 5. Transitions: Install heavy-duty, smooth transition strips at doorways and junctions with hard flooring, ensuring no trip hazards or door interference. 6. Furniture Handling: The Contractor shall systematically move and reset all furniture, desks, and storage fixtures. The Coast Guard will disconnect and secure computers, phones, personal effects, and sensitive records prior to work. 7. Refuse & Disposal: Bulk carpet waste and demolition debris shall NOT be disposed of in Coast Guard dumpsters; all bulk demolition materials must be removed and disposed of offbase in full accordance with environmental laws. Minor general work debris may use base dumpsters. 4.5 General On-Base Regulations & Security Colors: Morning colors (0800) and evening colors (sunset) require all outdoor personnel to face the flagpole, remain silent, and stop all vehicle/equipment movement. Traffic: Maximum base speed limit is 10 mph. No cellular phone usage while operating vehicles or equipment. Galley & Exchange: Contractors may purchase meals at the base galley (Breakfast 0600� 0730, Lunch 1100�1230) in clean work attire. Base Exchange access is permitted, excluding purchases of uniforms, alcohol, and tobacco. Firearms & Weapons: Strictly prohibited on USCG property. Personnel Background Check: Final contractor employee roster (Name, DOB, last 4 SSN) must be submitted at least one (1) week prior to project mobilization. 4.6 Warranty & Acceptance Workmanship Warranty: One (1) year from the date of final written acceptance covering all labor, installation defects, and remediation at zero cost to the Government. Manufacturer Warranty: Full commercial manufacturer warranties transferred to the USCG. Inspection & Cure: The Contractor shall provide at least 24 hours' notice before final inspection. Noted defects or punch-list items must be corrected within five (5) business days. 5. title: C1DA--523-418 B2 MH Addition - Construction Period Services
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This announcement is an Intent to Sole Source in accordance with FAR 6.103-5 Authorized or required by statute. It is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with William Pevear Architects, Inc, a Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), to provide Construction Period Services (CPS) during the construction project of Project #conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the 523-418 - B2 Mental Health Addition at the Brockton VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in Brockton, MA. PROJECT BACKROUND & DESCRIPTION: Our intention is to procure CPS in support of Project #523-418 - B2 Mental Health Addition Brockton VAMC, Brockton, MA 02301.The current design firm of record is William Pevear Architects, Inc located at 872 MASSACHUSETTS AVE STE 2-9, CAMBRIDGE, MASSACHUSETTS 02139. They are a VOSB and have been in the process of design this construction project since the award of the design contract 36C24121C0016 on March 29, 2021. The current design contract with William Pevear Architects, Inc no longer has CPS as part of the scope. The design is 100% complete and the construction procurement will be solicited in the near future. However, the project requires CPS in order to support the construction portion of this requirement. Any prospective design firm will need to possess working knowledge of all issues that may arise and will assume the liabilities associated with any and all aspects of the design. Throughout the solicitation period, the AE shall provide solicitation support services (SSS) to include, but not limited to attending the pre-bid site visit meeting and project walk, answering any technical questions/requests for information (RFIs) received from contractors within five calendar days of the date of the questions, and providing addenda as necessary if required to revise specifications and drawings. The AE shall provide CPS throughout the construction period to include, but not limited to, providing responses to any RFIs, reviewing submittals, creating a complete set of air emissions permit and land disturbance permit application forms, completing site visit reports, reviewing modification requests, completing a punch list and delivering record drawings. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a sole source continuation design contract to the original designer of record, William Pevear Architects, Inc. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330 (size standard $25.5 Million) applies to this procurement competitive. The duration of the project is estimated at a total period of performance of 950 calendar days, 120 calendar days for Construction Procurement and 730 calendar days for CPS. It is the intent of the Government to award this project as sole source. However, if a firm feels like they can meet the requirements of this project, the Government will review the information provided (as specified in the Capabilities below) in order to make a final determination. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 541310. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide examples of similar work your company has performed where you have taken over the responsibilities, and liabilities associated with any and all aspects of the design, for Solicitation Support Services and Construction Period Services from a design that was completed by another firm. Provide no more than three examples of this within the past seven years. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting this requirement may submit a capability statement to jacquelyn.wise@va.gov no later than December 18, 2026, at 1:00 PM (ET). It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than 4 single side pages that addresses the above information. This response must be submitted as a single application-generated (not scanned) PDF document that is less than or equal to 4MB in size. Please note that hard copies will not be accepted. A determination not to compete the requirement based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Disclaimer and Important Notes: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in responses to this notice. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for information provided in response to this notice. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for market research purposes. The Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. Contracting Office Address: VHA Program Contracting Activity Central (VHA-PCAC) 6100 Oak Tree Blvd. Suite 490 Independence, OH 44131 Primary Point of Contact: Jacquelyn Wise Contract Specialist Jacquelyn.wise@va.gov

title: Atomically Precise Molecules (APM)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the areas of new synthesis techniques for polymeric materials and nonlinear optical (NLO) materials. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in material synthesis with the ability to scale to quantities relevant for application integration, culminating in the development of a prototype demonstration of a revolutionary NLO material integrated into a functional government-provided electro-optic modulator. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice, or research that pivots on exceptional claims that cannot be technically justified in the proposal. This includes: � Proposals aiming to employ solely inorganic materials without a polymeric component � Proposals aiming to modify/repurpose existing NLO materials resulting in incremental improvements to the state-of-the-art (SoA)

title: Carpet Replacement at USCG Air Station Clearwater
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL SERVICES Solicitation Number: 20150PR270000020 Project Title: USCG Air Station Clearwater Carpet Replacement � FACENG and Supply Offices Issuing Agency: United States Coast Guard (USCG) � Base Miami Beach (Procurement & Contracting) Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside Applicable NAICS Code: 238330 � Flooring Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Acquisition Authority: FAR Subpart 12.6 (Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items), FAR Part 13 (Simplified Acquisition Procedures), and FAR Part 15 Performance Location: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater, 15100 Rescue Way, Clearwater, FL 33762 1. General Notice & Acquisition Overview This document constitutes a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services and minor facility improvements prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Sole Solicitation: This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Set-Aside: This solicitation is advertised as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. Offers received from entities other than small business concerns under NAICS code 238330 will not be considered. Basis of Award: Award will be made using simplified acquisition procedures to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all solicitation requirements and represents the Best Value to the Government, considering technical capability/approach, past performance, and price. 2. Schedule of Supplies / Services & Pricing The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, disposal, and incidental services necessary to complete the carpet replacement project as specified in the Statement of Work. CLIN Description Qty Unit Unit Price Total Amount 0001 Base Bid: Complete carpet replacement and cove base installation throughout FACENG and Supply Office spaces, including furniture moving/reset, weekend phasing, surface preparation, adhesives, transitions, and disposal (Approx. 2,820 SF Carpet / 775 LF Cove Base) in accordance with Project 33643384 SOW. 1 Job $____________ $____________ Note: Quantities are derived from drawing takeoffs and field estimates. Offerors are responsible for field-verifying all measurements during the pre-quote site visit prior to submitting their quote. 3. Site Visit Information A formal site visit has been scheduled for prospective offerors to inspect the existing site conditions, verify carpet and cove base dimensions, evaluate access routes, and inspect furniture configurations. Date & Time: Thursday, December 10, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST Location: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater 15100 Rescue Way, Clearwater, FL 33762 Primary COR: CWO Joe Calderon � Jose.A.Calderon@uscg.mil | Phone: (727) 423-7586 Alternate POC: LCDR Scott Kellerman � scott.n.kellerman@uscg.mil | Phone: (571) 499-0711 Required Security Submission for Site Visit: Real ID-compliant Driver�s License Number and State of Issuance Site Access Rules: Only U.S. citizens and permanent resident aliens are allowed onboard Air Station Clearwater. Attendees must present valid government photo identification at the front gate. Vehicles and equipment are subject to inspection at all times. 4. Statement of Work (SOW) � Project 33643384 4.1 Scope of Work Summary The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, materials, delivery, furniture moving, carpet and cove base removal, surface preparation, installation, cleanup, and disposal for the complete replacement of existing carpet and cove base throughout designated administrative areas within the FACENG and Supply building. All work must comply with the Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI) 104 Standard for Installation of Commercial Carpet, manufacturer written instructions, and applicable federal, state, and local standards. 4.2 Included Areas and Approximate Takeoffs FACENG and Conference Areas: Rooms 115, 116, 119, 122, former Room 114 suite (conference room, adjoining office, and internal passages): approximately 1,150 sq. ft. Supply Office Areas: Rooms 102, 103, 104, 107, 108, 109, and 110: approximately 1,670 sq. ft. Combined Planning Takeoff: Approximately 2,820 square feet of carpet tile and 775 linear feet of cove base. Excluded Areas: Hard-floor supply warehouse, public corridors/vestibules, main lobby, restrooms, mechanical rooms, and shop floors. Period of Performance: Total period of performance shall be forty-five (45) calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). Schedule Submission: The Contractor shall provide a phased, room-by-room work schedule outlining start dates, sequence, weekend milestones, and completion 4.4 Technical Requirements & Material Specifications 1. Carpet Tile: Commercial-grade, heavy/severe-traffic-rated modular carpet tiles equal to or exceeding existing durability and aesthetic standards. Materials must originate from consistent production runs/dye lots within each contiguous area. 2. Cove Base: Commercial resilient cove base matching existing height (minimum nominal height of 4 inches). 3. Submittals & Approval: Prior to material ordering, the Contractor must submit product technical data, adhesive specifications, color lines, transition details, and manufacturer warranty certificates to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). The COR will select final colors and patterns. 4. Subfloor Preparation: Remove old adhesive residue, perform mechanical scraping, patch cracks/depressions, and verify moisture and pH levels per manufacturer criteria before laying tile. 5. Transitions: Install heavy-duty, smooth transition strips at doorways and junctions with hard flooring, ensuring no trip hazards or door interference. 6. Furniture Handling: The Contractor shall systematically move and reset all furniture, desks, and storage fixtures. The Coast Guard will disconnect and secure computers, phones, personal effects, and sensitive records prior to work. 7. Refuse & Disposal: Bulk carpet waste and demolition debris shall NOT be disposed of in Coast Guard dumpsters; all bulk demolition materials must be removed and disposed of offbase in full accordance with environmental laws. Minor general work debris may use base dumpsters. 4.5 General On-Base Regulations & Security Colors: Morning colors (0800) and evening colors (sunset) require all outdoor personnel to face the flagpole, remain silent, and stop all vehicle/equipment movement. Traffic: Maximum base speed limit is 10 mph. No cellular phone usage while operating vehicles or equipment. Galley & Exchange: Contractors may purchase meals at the base galley (Breakfast 0600� 0730, Lunch 1100�1230) in clean work attire. Base Exchange access is permitted, excluding purchases of uniforms, alcohol, and tobacco. Firearms & Weapons: Strictly prohibited on USCG property. Personnel Background Check: Final contractor employee roster (Name, DOB, last 4 SSN) must be submitted at least one (1) week prior to project mobilization. 4.6 Warranty & Acceptance Workmanship Warranty: One (1) year from the date of final written acceptance covering all labor, installation defects, and remediation at zero cost to the Government. Manufacturer Warranty: Full commercial manufacturer warranties transferred to the USCG. Inspection & Cure: The Contractor shall provide at least 24 hours' notice before final inspection. Noted defects or punch-list items must be corrected within five (5) business days. 5. Quote Submission & Instructions to Offerors (FAR 52.212- 1 Addendum) 5.1 Submission Deadline & Contact Information Questions Due: Questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email no later than Monday December 14, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST

title: Atomically Precise Molecules (APM)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the areas of new synthesis techniques for polymeric materials and nonlinear optical (NLO) materials. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in material synthesis with the ability to scale to quantities relevant for application integration, culminating in the development of a prototype demonstration of a revolutionary NLO material integrated into a functional government-provided electro-optic modulator. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice, or research that pivots on exceptional claims that cannot be technically justified in the proposal. This includes: � Proposals aiming to employ solely inorganic materials without a polymeric component � Proposals aiming to modify/repurpose existing NLO materials resulting in incremental improvements to the state-of-the-art (SoA)
