title: Construction-NUWCDIVNPT-Interior Renovations
description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) has a commercial construction requirement for interior facility alterations and renovations. Under this firm-fixed-price completion effort, the contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, and quality control necessary to perform selective architectural demolition (removal of suspended ceilings, flooring down to concrete slab, interior doors, and select partitions) and complete renovation services�including new interior metal stud partitions with Level 5 gypsum wallboard finishes, acoustical ceiling systems with humidity-resistant tiles, vinyl composition tile (VCT) flooring with vinyl cove base, low/zero-VOC interior painting, heavy-duty interior double doors, and interior window units. The requirement further includes reconfiguring HVAC supply diffusers and return grilles, and providing complete electrical distribution upgrades (including a 45 kVA transformer, disconnect switch, and branch panels) to support baseboard convection heating, dimmable LED troffers, localized occupancy sensors, and emergency egress lighting. All work will be executed within an active, occupied military research facility under USACE EM 385-1-1 safety standards, lead-based paint remediation controls, asbestos containment awareness, and base security access requirements within a 120-calendar-day completion Period of Performance. description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) has a commercial construction requirement for interior facility alterations and renovations. UNICOR, Federal Prison Industries, Inc., is looking to procure an engraver with the following: Laser Cutter/Engraver System 1. Project Overview This Statement of Work defines the requirements, scope, deliverables, and acceptance criteria for the procurement, installation, and commissioning of a laser cutter/engraver system used for production applications, including cutting and engraving on metal, plastic, and glass. 1.1 Background The Federal Prison Industries program (now operating under the trade name UNICOR) was established in 1934 by an Executive Order issued by President Franklin D. Roosevelt. On January 1, 1935, FPI officially began operations as a wholly owned corporation of the United States Government. More than eighty-seven years after its establishment, the program continues to operate at no cost to taxpayers and benefits communities across the Nation creating safer prisons and reducing inmate recidivism. The mission of Federal Prison Industries, Inc. (FPI) is to protect society and reduce crime by preparing inmates with job training and practical work skills for reentry success. UNICOR restores lives by being a thriving corrections program that provides marketable skills and qualifications for inmates to succeed as productive citizens in our communities. We are a diverse, team-based organization where collaboration and respect for the capabilities of all staff and inmates is valued through work that is fulfilling. We deliver a competitive advantage in quality, on-time delivery, service, and cost in an innovative and safe environment that makes us the preferred supplier to our customers. UNICOR has strategic goals: - Maintain and develop meaningful work and job training opportunities to prepare inmates to become law-abiding citizens; � Ensure the corporation remains financially self-sustaining; � Prepare our staff to assume positions of greater responsibility by providing quality training and developmental opportunities. 2. Scope of Work The vendor will supply a complete laser cutter/engraver system in accordance with the specifications outlined below. The system must: � Use a CO? laser as the primary laser source. � Provide cutting capability for metals and plastics. � Provide engraving capability for plastic, metal, and glass. � Include a minimum 30-watt CO? laser. � Provide a minimum cutting/engraving area of 24 inches x 24 inches x 7 inches (XYZ). � Be compatible with CorelDraw for workflow integration. � Include a visual camera system for job alignment and material preview. � Dual-source systems (e.g., CO? + fiber) are acceptable and encouraged if beneficial. 3. Technical Requirements Laser System Specifications: � Laser Sources: Primary: CO? laser, minimum 30 watts. � Optional Secondary: Fiber or alternate laser type; vendor must specify wattage and purpose. � Cutting Capabilities: Metals: stainless steel, aluminum, mild steel (vendor must specify maximum thickness for each metal). �Plastics: acrylic, polycarbonate, ABS, and similar materials. � Engraving Capabilities: Must engrave consistently on metals, plastics, and glass. � Cutting Area Specification: Minimum usable working area of 24 inches (X) x 24 inches (Y) x 7 inches (Z). �Vendor must clearly state the maximum material thickness and Z-clearance supported. � Control & Software Requirements: Must be natively compatible with CorelDraw or include drivers/plugins enabling direct workflow integration; Support for standard design file formats (.DXF, .SVG, .AI, .PDF, CorelDraw-native formats). � Visual Camera System: o Integrated camera providing real-time preview, alignment assistance, and accurate visualization of material placement. � Motion/Control System: CNC or equivalent precision motion platform with production-grade accuracy and repeatability. � Safety Features: Fully enclosed or properly shielded system meeting applicable laser safety standards (e.g., ANSI Z136); Safety interlocks; emergency stop functions; and exhaust/filtration system. � Facility Requirements: Vendor must specify power, ventilation, cooling, and environmental requirements. 4. Deliverables Vendor will supply: � Complete laser cutter/engraver system meeting all specified requirements. � All necessary accessories, lenses, software, camera system, drivers, and safety equipment. � Delivery, installation, calibration, and commissioning at customer facility. � Operator training (minimum one in-person session). � Documentation including: User manuals � Maintenance procedures � Safety instructions � Warranty details 5. Project Timeline Vendor must provide a detailed timeline including: � Equipment production/preparation � Delivery date � Installation and commissioning schedule � Training schedule � Final acceptance testing date 6. Contract Performance 6.1. Period of Performance Best lead time and install time to begin support. Times will be used as an evaluation factor. Estimated time frame: 60 days 6.2 Place of Performance Machine and trainings will be delivered and performed at the following: UNICOR, 14601 Burbridge Rd SE, Cumberland, MD 21502 6.3 Access Hours Normal working hours at UNICOR are 7:00am � 3:00pm EST . title: Enterprise Workspace Management Support
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This notice is issued by the Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA HQ), on behalf of NAVSEA Facilities (Enterprise Workspace Management). NAVSEA is comprised of Headquarters (HQ) activities located at the Washington Navy Yard (WNY) and technical/industrial field organizations across more than 40 geographically dispersed activities spanning over 34 million gross square feet of facilities and supporting approximately 80,200 personnel. NAVSEA Facilities seeks to identify potential sources interested in and capable of fulfilling the requirements for enterprise workspace management support services to implement, sustain, expand, configure, and improve the ARCHIBUS Workplace Management System (IWMS) / Computer-Aided Facility Management (CAFM) platform. The current baseline utilizes ARCHIBUS version 25.2 (and approved upgrades) hosted across staging, testing, training, and production environments by the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) team at NSWC Dahlgren, VA. The requirement encompasses NAVSEA HQ, Program Executive Offices (PEOs), and participating field activities, including Naval Warfare Centers (NSWC/NUWC), Naval Shipyards (Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Portsmouth, Puget Sound), Regional Maintenance Centers (CNRMC, MARMC, SERMC, SWRMC), Supervisors of Shipbuilding (SUPSHIP Bath, Groton, Gulf Coast, Newport News), and related naval commands. (Incumbent Contract Reference: Currently satisfied under SeaPort Task Order N00178-14-D-8048-EH01 by BlueWater Federal Solutions, Inc. Estimated LOE is approximately 240,910 Direct Labor Hours over a 5-year period of performance: one 12-month base year plus four 12-month option years). This requirement may include the following efforts: Provide full lifecycle day-to-day ARCHIBUS system administration, user account lifecycles, security groups, Virtual Private Archives (VPAs), user roles, dashboard design, workflows, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Execute field-activity site rollout plans using Agile processes to incorporate stakeholder requirements, assess site constraints, deploy licensed modules, and deliver formal Site Rollout Completion Packages. Maintain capacity to execute rollouts at up to five (5) field activities simultaneously when surge capacity is required. Establish and validate data integrity, GeoHierarchies, and organizational structures linking personnel, room/cubicle space, telecommunications, and IT hardware assets. Perform authorized interior and exterior LiDAR/3D laser scanning, building feature surveys, and facility asset verification in accordance with Government CAD/BIM standards (e.g., USACE CAD Standards). Execute CAD polylining, drawing conversion, layer standardizations, and Building Information Modeling (BIM) publishing and integration into ARCHIBUS. Provide robust prime-contractor quality control, oversight, and deliverable validation for any subcontractor-performed survey, scanning, or CAD/BIM efforts prior to Government submission. Develop, test, and sustain automated daily data feeds between source systems, legacy databases, and the ARCHIBUS production database hosted in the Enterprise Digital Capabilities (EDC) environment. Prepare, package, and document Configuration Change Requests (CCRs), staging test scripts, release notes, user-impact assessments, and rollback plans, supporting testing and deployment from Navy Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) client environments. Facilitate stakeholder alignment sessions, business process mapping, and change-readiness activities across enterprise leadership and field activity commands. Develop role-based training curriculums, interactive guides, quick-reference aids, and SOPs; conduct hands-on training within the dedicated ARCHIBUS training environment prior to local go-live events. Accomplish full operational transition within a six (6) week phase-in period post-award, maintaining an Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), Quality Control Plan (QCP), and structured risk/issue registers. Ensure all personnel are U.S. citizens possessing a favorably adjudicated Federal Background Investigation at the Tier 3 (T3) level for Common Access Card (CAC) credentials and Navy IT network access. Maintain an adequate cost accounting system approved by DCAA/DCMA (FAR 16.301-3 / SF 1408) to support a CPFF task order.

title: Enlisted to Medical Degree Preparatory Program (EMDP2)
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or issuance thereof. Issued By: The Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU), Bethesda, Maryland Proposed NAICS Code: 611310 � Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools Proposed Product and Service Code (PSC): U005 � Education/Training - Tuition/Registration/Membership Fees USU is issuing this RFI to potentially identify capable sources and obtain information regarding the availability of contractors to support the requirements detailed below and in Attachment 1. Interested parties should refer to the Scope and Capability Statement Requirements sections for the specific information to include in their capability statement submissions. Background The Uniformed Services University (USU) of the Health Sciences is the nation's federal health professions academy. Its mission is to educate, train, and comprehensively prepare uniformed services health professionals, scientists, and leaders to support the Military and Public Health Systems, the National Security and National Defense Strategies of the United States, and the readiness of our Uniformed Services. USU comprises four schools: the School of Medicine (SOM), Graduate School of Nursing (GSN), Post Graduate Dental College (PDC), and the College of Allied Health Sciences (CAHS). To operate the DoD's only medical university, USU requires services to support military and civilian professors, instructors, administrative professionals, and students across diverse medical degree and certification programs. In 2014, USU partnered with the military services to develop and implement the Enlisted to Medical Degree Preparatory Program (EMDP2). EMDP2 enables highly qualified enlisted service members to complete a pre-medical post-baccalaureate program (PMPB) while maintaining their active-duty status in preparation for admission to medical school.

title: Acquisition SI
description: 1.0 Disclaimer & Important Notices This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and market research planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 and DFARS 212.70. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP), solicitation, or promise to issue an award or agreement. The Government will not pay for any information, documentation, or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the interested party's expense. Proprietary information, if any, must be clearly marked. The Government will handle proprietary materials in accordance with applicable federal statutes and regulations. Responding to this RFI does not grant any vendor competitive advantage or prejudice any future procurement. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future competitive solicitation or Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Call that may be issued. 2.0 Purpose & Mission Context The USSOCOM Directorate of Procurement (SOF AT&L-K) is conducting market research to determine industry interest and identify commercial partners with existing, commercially available Enterprise Acquisition Workflow and Super Intelligence Platforms ("Acquisition SI"). Currently, the acquisition environment involves disjointed documents, correspondence, approval routing, authoritative Government systems, and separate artificial intelligence tools. USSOCOM seeks to transition away from fragmented point utilities and prolonged custom software development models by procuring a mature, commercially established platform that natively integrates Super Intelligence across the acquisition lifecycle. The Directorate or Procurement seeks to understand what commercial solutions exist today that can deploy with minimal Government intervention to serve as a common operational workspace for Program Managers, Contracting Officers, Contract Specialists, Agreements Officers, Business Financial Managers (BFMs), and leadership. Key Objective: The Government is seeking information from commercial software providers capable of delivering a complete solution (either as a prime platform vendor or integrated commercial team) rather than disconnected point utilities. This notice signals USSOCOM's interest and benchmarks commercial market maturity across our key operational outcomes. 3.0 Core Operational Capabilities of Interest The Government is interested in commercial solutions that currently possess or can readily configure the following capabilities derived from our working Statement of Objectives (Not Attached): Cradle-to-Grave Multi-Pathway Execution: Managing an acquisition from requirement initiation and planning through document drafting, reviews, award, administration, and closeout across FAR/DFARS contracts and non-FAR instruments (specifically 10 U.S.C. �� 4021, 4022, and 4023 Other Transactions). Native Super Intelligence Assistance: Embedded, context-aware AI supporting document development (J&As, PNMs, IGCEs), regulatory compliance grounding (FAR, DFARS, SOFARS 5601, Class Deviations), and administrative checks while strictly preserving human-in-the-loop decision authority. Automated Compliance & PMR Audits: A dedicated compliance module capable of auditing contract files against agency checklists (such as the Directorate of Procurement DoW PMR Checklist) to support leadership reviews. Natural Language K SharePoint Discovery: Ability to query internal contract files and SharePoint repositories to locate existing vehicles, past awards, and vetted vendors to avoid duplicative buying. Government Enterprise Interoperability: Capable of secure data exchange with core acquisition systems (PIEE, SAM.gov, CCaR, Microsoft 365 / SharePoint Online). Open Architecture & Data Portability: Modular, open API architecture that avoids vendor lock-in, supports model agnosticism (plug-and-play foundation models), and guarantees full data export in standard open formats (JSON, CSV, PDF/A, XML). Cybersecurity & Network Onboarding: Cloud platform suitable for DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) operations, willing to actively support the USSOCOM J6 Authorization to Operate (ATO) onboarding process, with an architectural roadmap toward IL6. 4.0 Requested Information: Commercial Capability Statement To minimize the burden on industry while providing USSOCOM with actionable market intelligence, interested vendors are requested to submit a concise Commercial Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages) addressing the following areas: 1. Company & Commercial Solution Overview Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, UEI Number, and primary Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone). Business size status under NAICS 541512 / 513210 and identification of Non-Traditional Defense Contractor (NDC) status pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 3458 / � 4022. Name and description of your existing commercial platform, commercial availability date, and current operational customer base (specifically across DoD, federal agencies, or enterprise commercial clients). 2. Acquisition Lifecycle & AI Capabilities Core Workflow Coverage: Briefly describe how your commercial platform executes cradle-to-grave acquisition actions. Does your platform currently support both FAR-based contracts and non-FAR Other Transactions (OTs)? Native AI & Regulatory Grounding: Explain how AI is embedded into daily workflow tasks (e.g., document drafting, compliance verification, and routing). How does the system ensure outputs are grounded in authoritative regulations (FAR/DFARS)? Compliance & Discovery: Does your platform possess an automated compliance auditing capability (such as auditing against a checklist like the DoW PMR) and the ability to search internal document repositories (such as SharePoint) using natural language? 3. Enterprise Integration, Architecture, & Security Interoperability & Data Portability: Provide a high-level summary of your integration capabilities with DoD systems (PIEE, SAM.gov, CCaR, SharePoint). Confirm that Government data and workflows can be exported in open, non-proprietary formats without vendor lock-in. Cybersecurity & J6 ATO Posture: Describe your current hosting environment and DoD authorization status (e.g., FedRAMP, DISA IL4/IL5). State your ability and willingness to support the USSOCOM J6 Risk Management Framework (RMF) process to achieve an official Authorization to Operate (ATO). 4. Commercial Business & Licensing Model Provide an overview of your standard commercial licensing model (e.g., enterprise subscription, user-seat tiers, or transaction-based) and how AI compute/consumption is typically structured. (Note: Detailed cost proposals or binding pricing are not requested at this time.) 5.0 Submission Instructions & Points of Contact Format: Electronic submission in searchable Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word format, 11- or 12-point font, standard 1-inch margins. Page Limit: The complete response shall not exceed five (5) pages, excluding the title page. Submission Deadline: All responses must be received no later than 18 December 2026 at 1500 EST. Delivery Method: Submissions shall be emailed to the following points of contact with the subject line "RESPONSE: Acquisition SI Sources Sought - [Company Name]": POC 1: Regina.farrell@socom.mil POC 2: Joshua.t.myers.civ@socom.mil 6.0 Industry Exchanges & Demonstrations The Government may, at its discretion, invite select respondents to participate in one-on-one virtual discussions or commercial product demonstrations. The purpose of these sessions would be to gain a deeper understanding of current market capabilities, assess technical maturity, and inform acquisition strategy development.

This solicitation notice is for Fuel Operations Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Ft. Hood, TX. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Government as specified in Section C-2.0 Performance Requirements. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 493190 and will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. The period of performance is a four-year base period from December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2030, with a five-year option from December 1, 2030 through November 30, 2035, and a six-month option extension provision, December 1, 2035 through May 31, 2036. Hood SPE60326R0519 Amendment 0001 Clauses 10.13.2026 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). This is a follow-on solicitation notice to sources sought notice SPE603-25-R-5X24 and SPE603-25-R-0525. This solicitation notice is for Fuel Operations Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Ft. Hood, TX. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Government as specified in Section C-2.0 Performance Requirements. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 493190 and will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. The period of performance is a four-year base period from December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2030, with a five-year option from December 1, 2030 through November 30, 2035, and a six-month option extension provision, December 1, 2035 through May 31, 2036. The Government anticipates awarding one Firm-Fixed Price contract. This information is subject to modification and in no way binds the Government to award a contract.

description: A 100% Small Business Set-Aside solicitation will be issued to establish an Indefinite Quantity Contract (IQC) for NSN 1560-01-646-5441, a PANEL, STRUCUTRAL, AIRCRAFT. The award will be for a 5-year base period. The Estimated Annual Quantity (EAQ) is 40 EACH. Production units will be FOB: Destination; Inspection /Acceptance: Origin. Item is critical but not deemed a Critical Safety Item. Export Control applies. Surge does not apply. The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one or a limited number of sources under the authority of FAR 6.302. The OEM is Boeing (CAGE 81205) p/n 8-7849-11. Approved sources are H&R Parts Co. (CAGE 32821), Aero Components (CAGE 59213), Infinity Fabrication (CAGE 06DM5), Malones CNC Machining (CAGE 2V045) and DJ Engineering (CAGE 0C7H8). DLA Aviation does NOT possess complete technical data on this part. Any other interested manufacturing contractor would have to submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) package for approval to be added as a source by the assigned ESA. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within forty-five days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. This solicitation may include Procurement Note L09, Reverse Auction. Since a reverse auction may be conducted, offerors are encouraged to access the Procurex system and review the reverse auction help tutorials at https//dla.procurexinc.com to learn more about how to participate in an auction. In order to receive an award, regardless of dollar value, contractors must be registered in the System For Award Management (sam.gov). The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The estimated solicitation issue date is 11/16/2026. A copy of the solicitation will be available via DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. Choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requesters.

title: 6505--Nitroglycerin SL Tablets (VA-27-00011802)
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Enterprise Procurement Office intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0043 for an unrestricted procurement for Nitroglycerin Sublingual (SL) Tablets, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD) (inclusive of Tricare Mail Order Pharmacies (TMOPs)), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DOD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere on top of the successful offeror/contractor s label. Solicitation # 36E79727R0043 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 approximately November 27, 2026, with a tentative closing date of December 11, 2026. The NAICS code for this procurement is 325412. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at sam.gov. No paper copies of the solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the solicitation will be accepted. Interested offerors are advised to continuously check Contracting Opportunities at SAM.gov for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit an offer that if timely received, will be considered. The point of contact for this procurement is Alaina Anthony. Questions can be e-mailed to alaina.anthony@va.gov.
